notes.sowing: Sow {cm:2.5} deep from 3 weeks before your last frost. Each seed is a cluster that gives several seedlings, so thin to one every {cm:10} once they are about {cm:2.5} tall, and eat the thinnings.
notes.care: Water every week or so in dry spells; drought in the first 6 weeks often causes bolting and woody roots. Sow short rows every 3 weeks until midsummer, and about 10 weeks before your first fall frost for a fall crop.
notes.harvest: Pull roots at {cm:4} to {cm:7} across, between golf-ball and tennis-ball size; larger roots turn fibrous. Young leaves can be picked as greens. Lift fall roots before a hard freeze.
